title: Kosovo declares independence and Russia warns of a precedent for Abkhazia and South Ossetia
body:
On 17 February 2008 Kosovo declared independence from Serbia. More than 50 United Nations member states later recognised it, while Serbia and Russia opposed the declaration. Russian President Vladimir Putin had repeatedly warned that Kosovo could set a precedent for the so-called frozen conflicts of the post-Soviet space, among them Georgia's breakaway regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

In the weeks that followed, Moscow took several steps in relation to the two regions. On 6 March 2008 Russia unilaterally lifted the trade and other restrictions on Abkhazia that Commonwealth of Independent States leaders had imposed in January 1996. On 21 March the Russian State Duma urged the Kremlin to consider recognising Abkhazia and South Ossetia if Georgia joined NATO.

Georgia responded diplomatically. On 28 March 2008 Georgian President Mikheil Saakashvili unveiled a peace proposal offering Abkhazia what he called unlimited autonomy within Georgia. The Abkhaz president, Sergei Bagapsh, rejected the offer the same day. These exchanges, summarised in a Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty chronology of key events, formed the opening phase of the escalation that culminated in the war of August 2008.
